1.why: Clean sans-serif typeface with bold labels, comfortable line height and clear spacing between cards and fields throughout all steps.

2.why: No italics or all-caps sentences and body copy is short; only the dark monospace 'Logs' panel is a somewhat dense small-text block.

3.why: The layout is a single centred column that would likely reflow, but every screenshot is captured at desktop width (1280px) so mobile readability is not demonstrated.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Use your bank sign-in details to start MFA enrolment' and 'Create a test-only secret, then add it manually to your authenticator app' are one short plain sentence.

5.why: Only the mobile number field shows a format example (+44 7700 900000); the recovery code field and authenticator setup give no sample of expected input format.

6.why: Each card contains at most one or two short sentences, so no long passage must be read to proceed (the log panel is informational only).

7.why: The 32-character setup secret and the eight recovery codes are shown as plain text with no copy button, download or 'copy all' affordance.

8.why: Step 3/4 explicitly says to 'add it manually to your authenticator app'; no QR code or equivalent alternative appears anywhere.

9.why: Standard email and password input fields are used which password managers can usually fill, but no autocomplete hints, one-time-code fields or manager support are evident in the screenshots.

10.why: Each page has a large distinct heading and a single solid blue primary button, though the breadcrumb 'Sign in → Identity → Authenticator → Recovery codes' never highlights which step is current.

11.why: Most screens ask for one action (Sign in, Continue, Create secret, I saved these codes), although the settings screen presents three competing buttons at once.

12.why: Some confirmations are plain ('MFA is enabled. Save these one-time codes now.', 'Recovery code accepted. It cannot be used again.'), but after creating the secret no feedback states what happened or what comes next, and there is no clear post-verification summary.

13.why: The user can regenerate recovery codes, test a recovery code, and use a 'Back' button without penalty, though there is no reveal/hide toggle for the secret or codes.

14.why: The only error, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming but does not state what the problem was or how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown timers, expiry warnings or session clocks appear on any screen, implying unrestricted reading and entry time, though this is not explicitly stated.
